A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PuzzleFusion++ and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite the expanded appendix and renumbered displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original fracture-assembly results on Breaking Bad, including quantitative comparisons, iteration and sampling-step ablations, and qualitative results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds component ablations, verifier experiments, anchor-initialization statistics, and additional training and comparison experiments.

M1.justification: The encoder, 7D diffusion denoiser, anchor handling, pairwise verifier, losses, and iterative merging procedure remain the same in Section 3 and Appendix A.1. The revised pipeline diagram and new ablations explain and test existing components.

E1.justification: V2 adds the volume-constrained Everyday scenario, which excludes very small fragments and changes the represented input population (Appendix B.3). Artifact also becomes fine-tuning data rather than only test data. These are limited extensions within the retained Breaking Bad fracture-assembly task.

E2.justification: V2 adds substantive comparisons with PMTR and PHFormer in Tables 10–11 alongside the retained original baselines. Both introduce stronger rotation-error competitors. FRASIER is discussed through cited GeoTransformer results, rather than directly evaluated, so it is not counted as an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings remain, but v2 adds substantial evaluation designs: Artifact fine-tuning, training on volume-constrained Everyday data, denoiser component controls, and learned-versus-ground-truth verification. Verifier evaluation also introduces accuracy, precision, and recall at two thresholds. These additions do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's iteration and sampling-step studies, v2 tests scheduler, autoencoder, and anchor contributions; verifier thresholds and an oracle verifier; and anchor-initialization sensitivity. Appendix analyses add reconstruction diagnostics, scheduler comparisons, performance distributions by fragment count, and rotation-error analysis.

E5.justification: V2 Table 7 newly reports means and standard deviations across ten inferences with different anchor initializations. Figure 16 also displays performance distributions by fragment count. These are targeted statistical additions; repeated-training uncertainty remains unspecified for the main benchmark.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, while v2 adds extensive results. Examples include 82.9% PA with the oracle verifier versus 70.6% with the learned verifier, and 62.6% PA after Artifact fine-tuning with one iteration. New comparisons show worse rotation RMSE than PMTR and PHFormer under their respective reported settings. These are additions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The scheduler's second branch changes from m < t < T in v1 Figure 3 to m < t <= T in v2 Equation 1, explicitly defining the terminal timestep. This is a small formal correction; the underlying equations and losses are otherwise retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same auto-agglomerative contribution and broad performance claims, including the stated part-accuracy and Chamfer-distance advantages. These claims are not narrowed to reflect the additional rotation-error exceptions.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the diagnosis of limitations: verifier accuracy is affected by abundant negative pairs, low recall limits merging, and irreversible errors motivate backtracking. Appendix A.2 discusses alignment gaps missed by standard metrics, while Appendix B.4 proposes explanations and refinement directions for persistent rotation errors. V1's generalization discussion and principal failure modes remain.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code and models are available. Appendix A.2 explicitly documents use of the custom scheduler during both training and testing under DDPM. Existing hardware, training budgets, encoder specifications, and point counts remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted positioning against PMTR, PHFormer, FRASIER, and GeoTransformer in Appendix B.3, expands the contrast with DiffAssemble, and discusses DDPM versus EDM. These extend the comparison context while preserving the central positioning around PuzzleFusion and auto-agglomerative assembly.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. V2 clarifies anchor explanations, expands and subdivides the analysis narrative, changes citation and publication-header styling, adds acknowledgments, and removes the social-impact paragraph. The additions do not amount to a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redraws Figure 3 as an inference pipeline and adds numerous tables and figures for the new analyses. Figure 4 changes visualization alignment, removes one example, and revises its caption. Existing scheduler and appendix galleries are retained under new numbering, alongside extensive display relocation and conference-format layout changes.

improvement.justification: V1 offered limited direct validation of its distinctive denoiser components and verifier. V2 substantially strengthens that evidence through component ablations, oracle verification, initialization statistics, and additional competitive comparisons, while exposing important limitations. Incomplete details for the new training protocols and unchanged all-metrics wording despite rotation-error exceptions weaken the revision, but the gains in empirical support and diagnostic clarity are substantial.
